headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage via Continue’s filesystem/MCP bridge into a read-only documentation agent; no direct capability conflict or compliance breach is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or tool outputs. The python-cheatsheet agent is documentation-only and cannot itself inject, but it can become the content source that Continue parses as instructions. This is a plausible default pathway, not provably blocked.
conditions: IF Continue reads shared workspace files or MCP output as trusted instructions
IF the cheatsheet content is copied into a file that Continue later parses
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Keep the cheatsheet in a separate read-only workspace
Require explicit user confirmation before MCP tool calls
Add a provenance banner to imported content
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress, while the python-cheatsheet agent is documentation-only and touches no data classes. If both share the filesystem, Continue can expose workspace contents through its model provider or MCP path. The other agent does not add leakage capability, but the pair still creates a default shared-workspace exposure.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Continue sends buffer or file contents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive files into a different directory
Use a local-only model provider for Continue
Turn off broad network egress where possible
Open the cheatsheet in a non-shared workspace
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write access and multiple instances share state via the filesystem, but python-cheatsheet is runnable=false and has no write or filesystem capabilities. That makes overlapping mutable-resource conflict unlikely; the only plausible conflict is Continue-with-Continue, not between these two agents.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced by a writable agent
IF another Continue instance writes the same workspace concurrently
mitigations: Run only one Continue instance per workspace
Keep the cheatsheet repository read-only
Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory
Use git or filesystem locking
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP/tool outputs and edit code, but the python-cheatsheet agent is documentation-only and cannot take downstream actions. There is no evidence that Continue automatically treats the cheatsheet as authoritative, so the cascade is limited to manual copy/paste or explicit import, which keeps severity low.
conditions: IF a user copies cheatsheet text into Continue without verification
IF Continue is configured to execute tool actions from imported text
mitigations: Verify code suggestions before applying them
Disable auto-apply for edits
Keep documentation sources separate from task prompts
Require human review for MCP actions
requires-engineering: add citation/verification checks before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Continue handles model-provider API keys and workspace content, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no regulated data classes. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the shared workspace
IF a specific residency or retention policy is later attached to either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document data-handling policies before deployment
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
Review vendor compliance docs
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment
